findings.description: The bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration block, so objects are stored unencrypted by default rather than being automatically protected at rest.

findings.issue_category: no public access block / no explicit ACL
findings.description: No acl is set and no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is configured, leaving the bucket subject to default access settings that may allow unintended public access.
The bucket stores ledger export data (likely sensitive financial data) without any server_side_encryption_configuration, leaving it unencrypted at rest.
The bucket lacks a server_side_encryption_configuration block, so model artifacts are stored without encryption at rest.
The bucket lacks a server_side_encryption_configuration block, so operational runbooks (potentially containing sensitive operational details) are stored unencrypted.

The bucket uses the canned ACL 'log-delivery-write', which grants the predefined LogDelivery group write and read-ACP permissions; combined with no public access block, this can expose the audit trail bucket beyond the intended log-delivery service if not tightly scoped.

findings.issue_category: sensitive data uploaded to unencrypted bucket
findings.description: A vendor roster file (potentially containing sensitive vendor/business data) is uploaded to aws_s3_bucket.reports_archive, which has no encryption or access-block configuration, exposing the data to unauthorized access or plaintext storage.

force_destroy = true allows the bucket and all its contents to be destroyed without recourse, removing a safeguard against accidental or malicious data loss for what appears to be an archival/reporting bucket.

findings.issue_category: force_destroy enabled on sensitive data bucket
findings.description: force_destroy = true permits destruction of the bucket and its ledger export contents without additional protection, risking irreversible loss of financial records.
